perspective:
Vincent’s available information / subjective perspective:

- He is Vincent Chinana, an Alaska Native man, a mechanic, middle-school educated, with an ISTJ personality.
- He knows Patrick Guzman as a long-time friend since their teenage years. Patrick is a construction worker; they share a blue-collar bond and often collaborate, combining Vincent’s mechanical skills with Patrick’s construction expertise.

- At the diner, Vincent hears Patrick is considering a new construction venture. Patrick says it seems like a good opportunity to expand his business. Vincent says he has heard it is risky and asks if Patrick is sure. Patrick says he thinks it is worth the risk but is still weighing options. Vincent tells Patrick he is worried about financial security and suggests reconsidering or delaying until more information is gathered. Patrick thanks him and says he will think it over more.

- Later, at Patrick’s construction site, Vincent notices Patrick avoiding detailed discussion about the investment. Vincent tells Patrick they need to talk and says he feels Patrick is not telling him everything. Patrick says it is complicated and he did not want to worry Vincent with details. Vincent says that is exactly why they need to discuss it, that he is Patrick’s friend, and that he feels betrayed by the lack of transparency. Patrick apologizes, says he should have been more open, and agrees to sit down and explain everything.

- At Vincent’s garage, during their detailed discussion, Vincent learns the situation is serious. He hears Patrick say it has been tough and that Patrick might lose a significant amount if it does not turn around soon. Vincent offers to lend Patrick money to cover short-term losses. Patrick thanks him and accepts his support.

- At the coffee shop a month later, Vincent says the venture might actually turn a profit. Patrick says it is starting to look up and he is relieved they stuck with it. Vincent apologizes for doubting Patrick earlier and proposes a joint venture, saying he sees a lot of potential. Patrick agrees and says they should work out the details.

- At Vincent’s house, Vincent says that with both their skills combined, they can make it a success. Patrick agrees and says he is excited. Vincent suggests starting the business plan and outlining every step carefully. Patrick agrees they should cover all bases and set it up for success. Vincent participates in drafting the business plan.

Vincent does not have access to Patrick’s private thoughts or any hidden facts beyond what Patrick said and what Vincent directly observed.
